entries.title: Fuller summaries go deeper, with bold and bullets
entries.body: The Fuller summary runs to about 350 words in four to seven paragraphs and goes into the piece's method, evidence and limits. Brief and Fuller can put a key phrase in bold, and Fuller can use bulleted lists. Summaries you already have stay as they are until you regenerate them. On your own articles, a speech-bubble button beside each Brief or Fuller paragraph puts it into Chat, quoted, for you to ask about; nothing is sent until you press Send.

entries.title: Debate has two views: Reception and Claims
entries.body: Debate shows its sources in two views, each with a count. Reception lists pieces that link to or quote the article first, then those that match only its title, which used to be hidden by default. Claims groups sources under each claim, in the article's order. Debate's controls need the Experimental features switch on your profile page.

entries.title: Publication date and journal on the Metadata page
entries.body: Your own article's Metadata page shows its publication date and, when known, its journal. For a newly added paper with a DOI or arXiv number, the app checks public registries and, if title and author match, fills in a journal or a missing date, which also appears in your library's Published column. Existing articles are not looked up automatically.

entries.title: Highlights are yellow and saved by default
entries.body: Select text in one of your own articles and the note box opens with yellow already chosen (no colour in Referee mode). Closing the box saves the highlight and any note. Discard saves nothing, and copying the text then closing leaves no highlight behind unless you changed something.

entries.title: Dig deeper from a citation's pop-up card
entries.body: On your own articles, the card that appears when you point at a cited work has a Dig deeper button. Press it and the app starts looking further into that work, switches to Citations and scrolls to its row.

entries.title: Chat about a passage no longer covers it
entries.body: When the column of notes beside the article (Marginalia) is showing, the chat about a passage opens over that column rather than over the text, and the passage it is about gets a line down its right edge. Without that column, or on a phone or a narrow window, it floats as before.

entries.title: More room for search results; tapped cards stay
entries.body: In Search, the results list is taller: the key above it is gone, the note under the slider appears only when something is hidden, and saved searches take less space. On an iPad or other touch screen, a pop-up card opened with a tap stays open instead of closing at once.

entries.title: Chat keeps showing that it is working
entries.body: After the AI had finished a web search or other lookup, and before its first word arrived, nothing in Chat showed it was still working. The “thinking…” line with its spinner stays until the first word appears, and is larger and darker than before.
